verdicts.summary: The new filter covers only the fresh-arm branch. A child armed before its parent settled still auto-resumes at reset, and that resume is the one the commit says wakes the parent. Nothing re-checks the parent on that path.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A subagent child's run fails with a usage_limit error while its parent is active. 2) The sweep arms the child with limitRecovery{autoResume:true} through the fresh-arm branch (ProjectionStore.ts:3968-3984), which passes because the parent is not settled. 3) The user settles the parent before the reset time. 4) At reset, the first OR branch (ProjectionStore.ts:3958-3967) selects the child, because it has no parent check. 5) limitRecoveryCommand (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:29) checks only the child's own settledOverride, so it returns a message.dispatch 'Continue where you left off.' (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:57-78). 6) The child resumes. By the commit's own premise, this wakes the settled parent. A race gives the same result: the sweep reads the candidate, the parent settles, then autoArmLimitRecovery arms the child anyway, because it never re-checks the parent (Orchestrator.ts:13975-13998). I did not read the code that delivers a child's result to its parent, so whether the parent is actually woken is unverified. The test asserts the armed-child resume on purpose (diff test lines 157-191), so this may be a deliberate scope limit.
verdicts.consequence: A subagent of a parent settled after arming can still resume and re-engage the parent hours later. The fix covers only never-armed children.
